investigacion.base:
**Bottom line (as of Oct 5, 2026):** The question would resolve **NO** right now. No extension vote has happened, and I found no report that the new bills have been registered. The Rada has no plenary sessions until the week of Oct 12/13. In recent rounds the Rada has usually voted on the **Tuesday** of a plenary week, which points to Oct 13 or Oct 20 rather than Oct 15–17. That makes the timing uncertain.

**What the resolution sources say**
- **rada.gov.ua:** I couldn't load the live news feed. The latest Rada material I found is a transcript of the Sept 17, 2026 sitting, where Zhelezniak asked where the MPs were, since it was supposed to be a plenary day. Rada press releases confirm earlier extensions, for example on Oct 21, 2025 the Rada adopted bill No. 14128 in full.
- **Metaculus FAQ:** It only defines what counts as a "credible source." I didn't check it in detail.

**Status quo**
- On July 14, 2026, the Rada passed the 20th extension. 313 MPs voted for martial-law bill No. 15401 and 311 for mobilization bill No. 15402. Both now run from 05:30 on Aug 2, 2026 to 05:30 on Oct 31, 2026.
- Usual sequence: the president registers the two bills (the July bills were submitted July 13), the defence committee approves them, and the chamber passes them, sometimes the next day.

**Scheduled events**
- The Rada is holding no plenary sessions from Sept 17 to Oct 13. Reports say the next plenary week starts Oct 12, and other outlets say MPs return on Oct 13. Oct 13 is a Tuesday, so a normal Tue–Thu week would run Oct 13–15. Only Oct 15, the Thursday, falls inside the window.
- Zhelezniak linked the break to problems getting votes on some of Ukraine's international commitments and to financial difficulties. Attendance problems are possible, but extension votes have always passed comfortably.
- Oct 14 is Defenders' Day.

**Base rates and timing**
- All 20 extensions since Feb 2022 have passed, typically with 310+ votes, so passage is near certain. The open question is the date.
- Recent votes and how far ahead of expiry they came:
  - Oct 21, 2025 (Tuesday): 15 days before the Nov 5 expiry.
  - Mid-January 2026: before the Feb 3 expiry.
  - Apr 28, 2026 (Tuesday): 6 days before the May 4 expiry. The bills were registered Apr 27.
  - July 14, 2026 (Tuesday): 19 days before the Aug 2 expiry.
- Applied to the Oct 31 expiry, that puts a likely vote somewhere between about Oct 12 and Oct 27. The most likely dates are Tuesday Oct 13, the first day back, or Tuesday Oct 20 if the next plenary week is used. A vote on Oct 15 would need the bills to come up on the Thursday, or the week to be arranged differently.

**Prediction markets:** I didn't find any.

**What to watch:** when the bills are registered (likely Oct 6–13), when the defence committee approves them, Zhelezniak's Telegram for the plenary agenda, and whether Oct 20–22 is also a plenary week.

criterios: This question resolves YES if, on a plenary sitting day dated October 15, 16, or 17, 2026 (Kyiv local calendar), the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine adopts (passes by the required vote) at least one law extending the legal regime of martial law (voyennyi stan) and/or general mobilization (zahalna mobilizatsiya) in Ukraine beyond its current expiry of October 31, 2026. It resolves NO if no such law is passed by the full chamber on any of those three dates (for example, if the extension vote occurs on a different date, or has not yet occurred by the end of October 17, 2026). Resolution will be based on the Verkhovna Rada's official records and news feed at https://www.rada.gov.ua/ or on reporting from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) such as Ukrainska Pravda.
letra_pequena: Both the martial-law extension bill and the general-mobilization extension bill (typically registered as a pair) count; adoption of either one on one of the three qualifying dates is sufficient for YES. Only a final adopting vote by the full chamber counts — a committee recommendation, first-reading-only vote that does not adopt the law, or presidential signature on a different date does not by itself trigger resolution. The date used is the calendar date in Kyiv on which the Rada records the adopting vote.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About 10–12 days until the October 15–17 voting window; the outcome will be known after October 17 in Kyiv.

(b) **Status quo:** No qualifying extension vote has occurred or, as of October 5, been publicly scheduled. If that remains unchanged, the answer is **No**.

(c) **Reference class:** Ukraine has passed every martial-law and mobilization extension in this series, so eventual renewal is highly likely. But the relevant base rate is for the *date*: the recent documented votes cited were on Tuesdays, while this window runs Thursday through Saturday.

(d) **No scenario:** The Rada handles financing bills in its first week back and votes on the extensions on October 20, or votes earlier on October 13.

(e) **Yes scenario:** The president submits the bills in time for committee review, and the Rada adopts at least one on Thursday, October 15.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** Only the full chamber’s final adopting vote dated October 15, 16, or 17 **in Kyiv** counts. A vote on October 13 or 20 does not count, even if a presidential signature falls inside the window.

The narrow window, Tuesday precedent, and competing first-week agenda make **No** substantially more likely, despite the near certainty of an eventual extension.

Probability: 15%

(a) **Time left:** About 12 days, until the end of October 17 in Kyiv.

(b) **Status quo:** NO. No qualifying extension vote has occurred or been scheduled.

(c) **Reference class:** The Rada has passed every martial-law and mobilization renewal since 2022, but recent votes have often fallen on Tuesdays. That supports an eventual extension much more strongly than it supports a vote specifically on October 15–17.

(d) **NO scenario:** The Rada handles budget bills first and votes on the extensions on Tuesday, October 20—or votes on October 13.

(e) **YES scenario:** The president submits the bills during the first week back, and the Rada adopts at least one on Thursday, October 15.

(f) **Technicality:** Only the **final full-chamber adopting vote**, dated October 15, 16, or 17 in Kyiv, counts. Either extension law suffices; a later presidential signature does not change the vote date.

Probability: 17%

**(a) Time left:** The window closes at the end of October 17, 2026, about 12 days from now. The outcome will be known on October 15–17, or by the end of the 17th at the latest.

**(b) Status quo:** No vote has been held and no bills have been registered. If nothing happens on October 15–17, the question resolves NO.

**(c) Reference class:** All 20 previous extension rounds passed, so passage is near-certain and only the date matters.
- Recent votes cluster on Tuesdays: July 2024, October 2024, July 2025, October 2025, April 2026 and July 2026.
- A meaningful minority fell on a Wednesday or Thursday: January 2025, April 2025, and several in 2022–2023.
- Lead times before expiry have ranged from 6 to about 20 days.
- With an October 31 expiry, the vote could plausibly come anywhere from October 13 to about October 29.

**(d) NO scenario:** The president registers the bills around October 12. Either the Rada votes on Tuesday October 13 as its first item back, or the finance package crowds the first week and the extension slips to the next plenary week (October 20 or later). Both patterns fit recent practice.

**(e) YES scenario:** The first week back is filled with budget and financing bills on October 13. October 14 (Defenders' Day) is not a sitting day. The extension pair is then registered and cleared by committee in time for adoption on Thursday October 15 or Friday October 16.

**(f) Technicalities:**
- Only a final adopting vote on a date in Kyiv counts. Registration, a committee recommendation or a presidential signature does not.
- Either bill of the pair passing is enough.
- The window includes only one or two likely sitting days, October 15 and possibly 16. October 17 is a Saturday.
- Whether October 14 is a non-sitting day affects how the week is arranged.

**Estimate:**
- I put the chance of a vote in the first week back (October 13–16) at about 50%. The bills are still unregistered, and finance bills have priority, but past lead times of 15–20 days point to this week.
- If the vote is in that week, I put the chance it lands on October 15 or 16 rather than Tuesday October 13 at about 40–45%.
- That gives roughly 0.5 × 0.43 ≈ 21%.

Probability: 21%
